records.gloss: These [were the] sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah, Issachar and Zebulun,
pieces: These were the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

L.1: These [are] the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah, Issachar and Zebulun,

R.1: These were the sons of Israel, that is, Jacob: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob, the father of the twelve tribes
decisions.reason: Israel is the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 32:29). Chapter 1 traced the nations from Adam to Esau; here the lists turn to Jacob's twelve sons, the tribes whose families fill chapters 2-9.
The first six names are Leah's sons in order of birth (Genesis 35:23). Judah, fourth here, is the first tribe the following lists take up, because David's line comes from it.
Readable names Jacob so that young readers do not take Israel to be the nation here.

records.heading: The sons of Israel

records.source: דָּ֚ן יוֹסֵ֣ף וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן נַפְתָּלִ֖י גָּ֥ד וְאָשֵֽׁר׃ס
records.gloss: Dan, Joseph and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
pieces: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

L.2: Dan, Joseph and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

R.2: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

decisions.reason: Genesis 35:24-26 lists Rachel's sons Joseph and Benjamin, then Bilhah's sons Dan and Naphtali, then Zilpah's sons Gad and Asher. Here Dan comes before Joseph and Benjamin. The list does not say why; the twelve names are the same.

records.source: בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה עֵ֤ר וְאוֹנָן֙ וְשֵׁלָ֔ה שְׁלוֹשָׁה֙ נ֣וֹלַד ל֔וֹ מִבַּת־שׁ֖וּעַ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑ית וַיְהִ֞י עֵ֣ר׀בְּכ֣וֹר יְהוּדָ֗ה רַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וַיְמִיתֵֽהוּ׃ס
records.gloss: [The] sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah; three [were] born to him from Bath-shua the Canaanite. And was Er, [the] firstborn of Judah, evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and he put him to death.
pieces: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan and Shelah. Bath-shua, a Canaanite woman, was the mother of these three. But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s eyes, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought his life to an end.

L.3: [The] sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah; [these] three were born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite [woman]. And Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put him to death.

R.3: The sons of Judah were Er, Onan and Shelah. Their mother was Bath-shua, a Canaanite woman. Er, Judah's oldest son, did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw as evil, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} caused him to die.

decisions.reason: Genesis 38:2 and 38:12 call Judah's wife the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite. Here the same words serve as her name.

decisions.choice: Er was evil ... and he put him to death: Genesis 38:7
decisions.reason: The words follow Genesis 38:7 (see the decisions there, including the play between the name Er and the word for "evil"). Genesis repeats the LORD as subject of the second verb; Chronicles only says "he", but the LORD is meant. Onan's death (Genesis 38:10) is not mentioned.

decisions.choice: the LORD caused him to die
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as subject, as Genesis 38:7 does, instead of a pronoun.

records.heading: The descendants of Judah

records.source: וְתָמָר֙ כַּלָּת֔וֹ יָ֥לְדָה לּ֖וֹ אֶת־פֶּ֣רֶץ וְאֶת־זָ֑רַח כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה חֲמִשָּֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And Tamar his daughter-in-law bore to him Perez and Zerah. All [the] sons of Judah: five.
pieces: His daughter-in-law Tamar bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.

L.4: And Tamar his daughter-in-law bore to him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah [were] five.

R.4: Judah's daughter-in-law Tamar also had sons by him, Perez and Zerah. So Judah had five sons in all.

decisions.choice: Tamar his daughter-in-law: the story of Genesis 38
decisions.reason: Tamar was the widow of Er. Genesis 38 tells how she bore Judah twins, Perez and Zerah (38:27-30). The list names her without comment; the line of Perez leads to David (Ruth 4:12, 18-22).
The total counts the two sons who died (verse 3; Genesis 46:12) as well as Shelah, Perez and Zerah.

records.source: בְּנֵי־פֶ֖רֶץ חֶצְר֥וֹן וְחָמֽוּל׃ס
records.gloss: [The] sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
pieces: The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

L.5: [The] sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

R.5: The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

decisions.reason: The same two sons appear in Genesis 46:12 and Numbers 26:21. Hezron's line is followed from verse 9.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י זֶ֗רַח זִ֠מְרִי וְאֵיתָ֧ן וְהֵימָ֛ן וְכַלְכֹּ֥ל וָדָ֖רַע כֻּלָּ֥ם חֲמִשָּֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Zerah: Zimri and Ethan and Heman and Calcol and Dara; all of them five.
pieces: The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara, five in all.

L.6: And [the] sons of Zerah: Zimri and Ethan and Heman and Calcol and Dara; all of them, five.

R.6: The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara. There were five of them.

decisions.choice: Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara: the wise men of 1 Kings 5:11
alternatives: different men with the same names
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 5:11 names Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol and Darda as men famous for wisdom. Dara and Darda differ by one letter, and "Ezrahite" may mean a descendant of Zerah, so the same men are probably meant, though Kings calls them sons of Mahol.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י כַּרְמִ֑י עָכָר֙ עוֹכֵ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָעַ֖ל בַּחֵֽרֶם׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Carmi: Achar, troubler of Israel, who acted unfaithfully in the devoted thing.
pieces: The son of Carmi: Achar, the one who brought trouble on Israel by breaking faith over the devoted things.

L.7: And [the] sons of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who committed a breach of faith in the devoted thing.

R.7: Carmi's son was Achar, who brought trouble on Israel. He was unfaithful by taking some of the devoted things, the things that belonged to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone.

decisions.choice: Achar, the troubler: a play on his name
decisions.reason: Joshua 7 calls this man Achan. Here he is Achar, which sounds like the verb "to trouble" ('akhar) used of him in Joshua 7:25 ("Why have you troubled us?"), where the place of his death is named the Valley of Achor (7:26). The spelling ties his name to what he did.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully in the devoted thing: Joshua 7:1
decisions.reason: The words repeat Joshua 7:1, where Achan took goods from Jericho that were devoted to the LORD (see the decisions there). Joshua 7:1 calls Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah; Zabdi is probably Zimri of verse 6, a near form of the same name.

decisions.choice: son, not sons, before a single name
decisions.reason: The list heading is plural ("sons of") even when one name follows. Balanced and Readable use the singular there, which is how English says it; Literal keeps the plural.

decisions.choice: the things that belonged to the LORD alone
decisions.reason: Readable explains the devoted things as Joshua 7:1 does.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י אֵיתָ֖ן עֲזַרְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Ethan: Azariah.
pieces: The son of Ethan: Azariah.

decisions.choice: sons of with one name: a fixed heading
decisions.reason: The list keeps its usual heading even when only one son is named; it does not mean that others were left out.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י חֶצְר֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר נוֹלַד־ל֑וֹ אֶת־יְרַחְמְאֵ֥ל וְאֶת־רָ֖ם וְאֶת־כְּלוּבָֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Hezron who were born to him: Jerahmeel and Ram and Chelubai.
pieces: The sons born to Hezron: Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai.

L.9: And [the] sons of Hezron who were born to him: Jerahmeel and Ram and Chelubai.

R.9: The sons of Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai.

decisions.choice: Chelubai: another form of the name Caleb
decisions.reason: Chelubai is the Caleb son of Hezron of verses 18 and 42. He is not Caleb son of Jephunneh, the spy of Numbers 13:6, who lived several generations later (see verses 18 and 49).
The three sons are followed in turn: Ram's line to David (verses 10-17), Caleb's family (18-24), Jerahmeel's (25-41), and more of Caleb's (42-55).

records.source: וְרָ֖ם הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־עַמִּינָדָ֑ב וְעַמִּינָדָב֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־נַחְשׁ֔וֹן נְשִׂ֖יא בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Ram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, leader of [the] sons of Judah.
pieces: Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, the leader of the people of Judah.

L.10: And Ram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, leader of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah.

R.10: Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was the leader of the tribe of Judah.

decisions.choice: Ram to David: the line of Ruth 4:19-22
decisions.reason: Verses 10-15 give the same line as Ruth 4:19-22. Nahshon was the leader of Judah in the wilderness (Numbers 1:7; 2:3; 7:12).

decisions.choice: begot: became the father or ancestor of
decisions.reason: This verb is the formula of the family lists. It can name a grandfather or later ancestor as well as a father, so a list may skip generations.

decisions.choice: begot (Literal), was the father of (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: One wording for this formula at each level throughout the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 1-9; Ruth 4 has "fathered" for the same verb.

records.source: וְנַחְשׁוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־שַׂלְמָ֔א וְשַׂלְמָ֖א הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־בֹּֽעַז׃
records.gloss: And Nahshon begot Salma, and Salma begot Boaz.
pieces: Nahshon was the father of Salma, and Salma was the father of Boaz.

L.11: And Nahshon begot Salma, and Salma begot Boaz.

R.11: Nahshon was the father of Salma, and Salma was the father of Boaz.

decisions.choice: Salma: Salmah and Salmon in Ruth
decisions.reason: Ruth 4:20 spells this name Salmah and Ruth 4:21 Salmon; Chronicles has Salma. They are forms of one name for one man. A Salma also appears in verses 51 and 54 as father of Bethlehem.

records.source: וּבֹ֨עַז֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־עוֹבֵ֔ד וְעוֹבֵ֖ד הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־יִשָֽׁי׃
records.gloss: And Boaz begot Obed, and Obed begot Jesse.
pieces: Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.

L.12: And Boaz begot Obed, and Obed begot Jesse.

R.12: Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.

decisions.reason: Obed was the son of Boaz and Ruth the Moabite (Ruth 4:13-17).

records.source: וְאִישַׁ֛י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־בְּכֹר֖וֹ אֶת־אֱלִיאָ֑ב וַאֲבִינָדָב֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְשִׁמְעָ֖א הַשְּׁלִישִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: And Jesse begot his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third,
pieces: Jesse was the father of Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,

L.13: And Jesse begot his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third,

R.13: Jesse was the father of Eliab, his oldest son. His second son was Abinadab, and his third was Shimea.

decisions.choice: Jesse: spelled here with an extra first letter
decisions.reason: Only here is Jesse's name written with an added first letter ('Ishay); it is the same man as in verse 12.

The first three sons are the ones who passed before Samuel in 1 Samuel 16:6-9 and went to war against the Philistines in 17:13. Shimea is called Shammah there and Shimeah in 2 Samuel 13:3: forms of one name.

records.source: נְתַנְאֵל֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔י רַדַּ֖י הַחֲמִישִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
pieces: Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,

L.14: Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,

R.14: His fourth son was Nethanel, and his fifth was Raddai.

decisions.reason: These two sons of Jesse are named only here.

records.source: אֹ֚צֶם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י דָּוִ֖יד הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃
records.gloss: Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.
pieces: Ozem the sixth and David the seventh.

L.15: Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.

R.15: His sixth son was Ozem, and his seventh was David.

decisions.choice: David the seventh: 1 Samuel 16:10-11 implies eight sons
alternatives: David was the eighth son, one being left out here
decisions.reason: In 1 Samuel 16:10-11 Jesse makes seven of his sons pass before Samuel while David is still with the flock, and 1 Samuel 17:12 says Jesse had eight sons. Chronicles names seven, with David last. One son may have died without children and so dropped out of the family record; the text does not say.
Readable turns each ordinal into a short sentence, as in verses 13-14.

records.source: וְאַחְיוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם צְרוּיָ֣ה וַאֲבִיגָ֑יִל וּבְנֵ֣י צְרוּיָ֗ה אַבְשַׁ֛י וְיוֹאָ֥ב וַעֲשָׂה־אֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And their sisters: Zeruiah and Abigail. And [the] sons of Zeruiah: Abishai and Joab and Asahel, three.
pieces: Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab and Asahel, three of them.

L.16: And their sisters [were] Zeruiah and Abigail. And [the] sons of Zeruiah: Abishai and Joab and Asahel, three.

R.16: Jesse's sons also had two sisters, Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's three sons were Abishai, Joab and Asahel.

decisions.choice: Abishai, Joab and Asahel: David's nephews
decisions.reason: Zeruiah's three sons were David's warriors and Joab his commander (2 Samuel 2:18; 8:16). They are always named by their mother; their father is never named (2 Samuel 2:32 mentions his tomb in Bethlehem). The name Abishai is written here in a shorter form (Abshai).

decisions.choice: their sisters: David's sisters or half-sisters
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 17:25 calls Abigail the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah. They may have been half-sisters of Jesse's sons; see the decisions there.
Readable says whose sisters they were.

records.source: וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל יָלְדָ֖ה אֶת־עֲמָשָׂ֑א וַאֲבִ֣י עֲמָשָׂ֔א יֶ֖תֶר הַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And Abigail bore Amasa; and [the] father of Amasa [was] Jether the Ishmaelite.
pieces: Abigail bore Amasa, and Amasa's father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

L.17: And Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa [was] Jether the Ishmaelite.

R.17: Abigail was the mother of Amasa. Amasa's father was Jether, an Ishmaelite.

decisions.choice: Jether the Ishmaelite: "Ithra the Israelite" in 2 Samuel 17:25
decisions.reason: Jether and Ithra are two forms of one name. 2 Samuel 17:25 calls him "the Israelite"; Chronicles says "the Ishmaelite", which would explain why his people are mentioned at all (see the decision at 2 Samuel 17:25). The Hebrew of Chronicles is followed here.
Amasa led Absalom's army against David (2 Samuel 17:25), later became David's commander, and was killed by his cousin Joab (2 Samuel 20:10).

records.source: וְכָלֵ֣ב בֶּן־חֶצְר֗וֹן הוֹלִ֛יד אֶת־עֲזוּבָ֥ה אִשָּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־יְרִיע֑וֹת וְאֵ֣לֶּה בָנֶ֔יהָ יֵ֥שֶׁר וְשׁוֹבָ֖ב וְאַרְדּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And Caleb son of Hezron begot Azubah, a wife, and Jerioth; and these [were] her sons: Jesher and Shobab and Ardon.
pieces: Caleb son of Hezron had children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth. Her sons were Jesher, Shobab and Ardon.

L.18: And Caleb son of Hezron begot [children] by Azubah, [his] wife, and by Jerioth; and these [are] her sons: Jesher and Shobab and Ardon.

R.18: Caleb son of Hezron had children with his wife Azubah and with Jerioth. Her sons were Jesher, Shobab and Ardon.

decisions.choice: fathered children by Azubah and by Jerioth
alternatives: Caleb fathered Jerioth by his wife Azubah
decisions.reason: Word for word the Hebrew says Caleb "fathered Azubah, a wife, and Jerioth", but this verb normally takes the child as its object. It is read here as fathering children by the two women. Others take Jerioth as a daughter of Caleb and Azubah, or as Azubah's other name. "Her sons" most likely means Azubah's, who is named again in verse 19.

decisions.choice: Caleb son of Hezron: one of several Calebs
decisions.reason: This Caleb (Chelubai in verse 9) is Judah's great-grandson. Caleb son of Jephunneh, the spy who took Hebron (Numbers 13:6; Joshua 14:13-14), lived in Moses' time. The family of this earlier Caleb holds towns linked with the later one (Hebron in verse 42, Achsah in verse 49), and verse 42 speaks of Caleb "the brother of Jerahmeel"; the lists do not say how the Calebs are related.
English needs the word "children" for the sense in m1.

records.source: וַתָּ֖מָת עֲזוּבָ֑ה וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֤וֹ כָלֵב֙ אֶת־אֶפְרָ֔ת וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ אֶת־חֽוּר׃
records.gloss: And died Azubah, and took for himself Caleb Ephrath, and she bore to him Hur.
pieces: When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, and she bore him Hur.

L.19: And Azubah died, and Caleb took Ephrath for himself, and she bore to him Hur.

R.19: After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, and they had a son named Hur.

decisions.reason: "Took" a woman for oneself means took her as wife.
Ephrath, also Ephrathah (verses 24 and 50), is a name tied to Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19; Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:1). Her son Hur is the ancestor of the founder of Bethlehem (verses 50-51).

records.source: וְחוּר֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־אוּרִ֔י וְאוּרִ֖י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־בְּצַלְאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And Hur begot Uri, and Uri begot Bezalel.
pieces: Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.

L.20: And Hur begot Uri, and Uri begot Bezalel.

R.20: Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.

decisions.choice: Bezalel: the craftsman of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, was the man the LORD chose to make the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 31:2; 35:30).

records.source: וְאַחַ֗ר בָּ֤א חֶצְרוֹן֙ אֶל־בַּת־מָכִיר֙ אֲבִ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד וְה֣וּא לְקָחָ֔הּ וְה֖וּא בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ אֶת־שְׂגֽוּב׃
records.gloss: And afterward went in Hezron to [the] daughter of Machir, father of Gilead, and he took her, and he [was] a son of sixty years; and she bore to him Segub.
pieces: Later Hezron lay with the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he took as his wife at the age of sixty. She bore him Segub.

L.21: And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, and he took her when he [was] sixty years old; and she bore to him Segub.

R.21: Later, when Hezron was sixty years old, he married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead. She had a son by him named Segub.

decisions.choice: went in to ... took her: married and lived with her
decisions.reason: "Went in to" a woman speaks of sexual union; "took her" shows that it was in marriage.

decisions.choice: Machir the father of Gilead: Manasseh's family
decisions.reason: Machir was the son of Manasseh and the ancestor of the people of Gilead, east of the Jordan (Numbers 26:29; 32:39-40). Through this marriage a family of Judah was joined to Manasseh.
Readable puts the age first so the order of events is plain.

records.source: וּשְׂג֖וּב הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־יָאִ֑יר וַֽיְהִי־ל֗וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלוֹשׁ֙ עָרִ֔ים בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And Segub begot Jair, and belonged to him twenty-three cities in [the] land of the Gilead.
pieces: Segub was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.

L.22: And Segub begot Jair, and he had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

R.22: Segub was the father of Jair. Jair had twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.

decisions.choice: Jair: called a son of Manasseh in Numbers
decisions.reason: Numbers 32:41 and Deuteronomy 3:14 call Jair a son of Manasseh, who took villages in Gilead and named them after himself. Chronicles shows that his grandmother was of Manasseh's family and his father's line was Judah.
The word covers settlements of any size; "towns" suits places in a country district.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח גְּשֽׁוּר־וַ֠אֲרָם אֶת־חַוֺּ֨ת יָאִ֧יר מֵאִתָּ֛ם אֶת־קְנָ֥ת וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים עִ֑יר כָּל־אֵ֕לֶּה בְּנֵ֖י מָכִ֥יר אֲבִי־גִלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: And took Geshur and Aram the villages of Jair from them, Kenath and its daughters, sixty cities. All these [were the] sons of Machir, father of Gilead.
pieces: But Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-jair from them, with Kenath and its villages, sixty towns. All these were descendants of Machir the father of Gilead.

L.23: And Geshur and Aram took the villages of Jair from them, Kenath and its daughters, sixty cities. All these [were the] sons of Machir the father of Gilead.

R.23: But the kingdoms of Geshur and Aram took the villages of Jair from them, together with Kenath and the villages around it, sixty towns in all. All these people were descendants of Machir, the father of Gilead.

decisions.choice: Geshur and Aram: kingdoms to the north
decisions.reason: Geshur and Aram were Aramean kingdoms north and east of Gilead (2 Samuel 3:3; 15:8). The list does not say when they took these towns.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that belonged to a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the smaller settlements around it.
"All these" are the people of verses 21-23, Machir's descendants through his daughter.
Balanced uses the place name, "villages of Jair", as Numbers 32:41 does.

records.source: וְאַחַ֥ר מוֹת־חֶצְר֖וֹן בְּכָלֵ֣ב אֶפְרָ֑תָה וְאֵ֤שֶׁת חֶצְרוֹן֙ אֲבִיָּ֔ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֶת־אַשְׁח֖וּר אֲבִ֥י תְקֽוֹעַ׃
records.gloss: And after [the] death of Hezron in Caleb-ephrathah, and [the] wife of Hezron [was] Abijah, and she bore to him Ashhur, father of Tekoa.
pieces: After Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.

L.24: And after the death of Hezron in Caleb-ephrathah, the wife of Hezron [was] Abijah, and she bore to him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.

R.24: After Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah gave birth to his son Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa.

decisions.choice: after Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore him Ashhur
alternatives: after Hezron died, Caleb went in to Ephrathah, the wife of Hezron his father, and she bore him Ashhur
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is unusual: a place named Caleb-ephrathah appears nowhere else, and the son is born after his father's death. The early Greek translation reads "after Hezron died, Caleb went in to Ephrathah", and some take Abijah to be a word for "his father", so that Caleb took his father's widow. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: father of a town: its founder, or the head of the clan that settled it
decisions.reason: When a man is called "father of" a town (here Tekoa, south of Bethlehem: 2 Samuel 14:2; Amos 1:1), he is its founder or the ancestor and head of the clan that lived there. The same title comes back many times in chapters 2, 4, 8 and 9. In a few places it is not certain whether the name after "father of" is a town or a person who bore a town's name.
Readable explains "father of" a town (m2) with one word, here and wherever the title recurs in chapters 2-9. Literal and Balanced keep "father of", which leaves room for the other reading.

records.source: וַיִּהְי֧וּ בְנֵי־יְרַחְמְאֵ֛ל בְּכ֥וֹר חֶצְר֖וֹן הַבְּכ֣וֹר׀רָ֑ם וּבוּנָ֥ה וָאֹ֛רֶן וָאֹ֖צֶם אֲחִיָּֽה׃

pieces: The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron: Ram the firstborn, then Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah.

L.25: And [the] sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were: the firstborn Ram, and Bunah and Oren and Ozem, Ahijah.

R.25: Jerahmeel was Hezron's oldest son. His sons were Ram, the oldest, then Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah.

decisions.reason: There is no "and" before Ahijah, so some read "by Ahijah", the name of Jerahmeel's first wife, which would fit "another wife" in verse 26. As the text stands Ahijah is listed among the sons.
He is the nephew of Ram the ancestor of David (verses 9-10). Names often recur within a family.

pieces: Jerahmeel had another wife, named Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.

L.26: And Jerahmeel had another wife, and her name [was] Atarah; she [was the] mother of Onam.

R.26: Jerahmeel also had another wife named Atarah. She was Onam's mother.

decisions.reason: Jerahmeel had more than one wife. The sons of verse 25 were by the first, unnamed unless she is Ahijah (verse 25); Onam's line follows in verses 28-33.

R.27: The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel's oldest son, were Maaz, Jamin and Eker.

decisions.reason: As in verse 25: not the Ram of verse 10.

L.28: And [the] sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. And [the] sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.

R.28: The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.

decisions.reason: This Shammai, of Jerahmeel's family, is not the Shammai of verses 44-45 in Caleb's family.

pieces: Abishur's wife was named Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.

L.29: And the name of the wife of Abishur [was] Abihail, and she bore to him Ahban and Molid.

R.29: Abishur's wife was Abihail. She had two sons by him, Ahban and Molid.

decisions.reason: The same name is a man's in Numbers 3:35. The list names mothers where they matter to the family line.

pieces: The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. Seled died without sons.

L.30: And [the] sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; and Seled died without sons.

R.30: The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim. Seled died without having any sons.

decisions.reason: The word can mean children in general, but verse 34 sets sons against daughters, and the point is that his line ends with him.

pieces: The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The descendant of Sheshan: Ahlai.

L.31: And [the] sons of Appaim: Ishi. And [the] sons of Ishi: Sheshan. And [the] sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.

R.31: Appaim's son was Ishi, and Ishi's son was Sheshan. Sheshan's descendant was Ahlai.

decisions.choice: Ahlai: a descendant of Sheshan, not a son
alternatives: Ahlai a son born after verse 34
decisions.reason: Verse 34 says Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. So Ahlai was either a daughter, perhaps the one given to Jarha (verse 35), or a grandson through her. A Zabad son of Ahlai is among David's warriors (11:41); compare Zabad in verse 36.
In view of m1, Balanced and Readable do not say "son" for Ahlai; for Ishi and Sheshan they say "son", as in verse 7.

pieces: The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without sons.

L.32: And [the] sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; and Jether died without sons.

R.32: The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother, were Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without having any sons.

decisions.reason: As in verse 30. This Jether is not the Jether of verse 17.

pieces: The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the descendants of Jerahmeel.

L.33: And [the] sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.

R.33: The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. All these were descendants of Jerahmeel.

decisions.reason: The closing line covers the whole family of verses 25-33. Verses 34-41 then add Sheshan's line in more detail.
In a closing line of a list "sons" means descendants, and Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־הָיָ֧ה לְשֵׁשָׁ֛ן בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־בָּנ֑וֹת וּלְשֵׁשָׁ֛ן עֶ֥בֶד מִצְרִ֖י וּשְׁמ֥וֹ יַרְחָֽע׃
records.gloss: And not belonged to Sheshan sons, but only daughters; and to Sheshan [was] a slave, Egyptian, and his name [was] Jarha.
pieces: Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. But Sheshan had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.

L.34: And Sheshan had no sons, only daughters; and Sheshan had an Egyptian slave, and his name [was] Jarha.

R.34: Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had a servant from Egypt named Jarha.

decisions.reason: Jarha belonged to Sheshan as a member of his household; he was not a hired worker.
As the style of this translation sets out for this word, Literal says "slave" and Balanced and Readable "servant" (m1).

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שֵׁשָׁ֧ן אֶת־בִּתּ֛וֹ לְיַרְחָ֥ע עַבְדּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ אֶת־עַתָּֽי׃
records.gloss: And gave Sheshan his daughter to Jarha his slave for a wife, and she bore to him Attai.
pieces: Sheshan gave his daughter as a wife to his servant Jarha, and she bore him Attai.

L.35: And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his slave as a wife, and she bore to him Attai.

R.35: Sheshan let his daughter marry his servant Jarha, and she had a son by him named Attai.

decisions.choice: a daughter married to a household servant
decisions.reason: A man with no sons could keep his line and his land in the family by marrying his daughter to a man of his own household; her children counted as his descendants. Compare the daughters of Zelophehad (Numbers 27:1-11; 36:1-12).

records.source: וְעַתַּי֙ הֹלִ֣יד אֶת־נָתָ֔ן וְנָתָ֖ן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־זָבָֽד׃
records.gloss: And Attai begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad.
pieces: Attai was the father of Nathan, and Nathan was the father of Zabad.

L.36: And Attai begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad.

R.36: Attai was the father of Nathan, and Nathan was the father of Zabad.

decisions.reason: A Zabad son of Ahlai is among David's warriors (11:41); if Ahlai was Sheshan's daughter (verse 31), he may be this Zabad.

records.source: וְזָבָד֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־אֶפְלָ֔ל וְאֶפְלָ֖ל הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עוֹבֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And Zabad begot Ephlal, and Ephlal begot Obed.
pieces: Zabad was the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal was the father of Obed.

L.37: And Zabad begot Ephlal, and Ephlal begot Obed.

R.37: Zabad was the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal was the father of Obed.

decisions.reason: Not Obed son of Boaz (verse 12); the name was common.

records.source: וְעוֹבֵד֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־יֵה֔וּא וְיֵה֖וּא הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עֲזַרְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Obed begot Jehu, and Jehu begot Azariah.
pieces: Obed was the father of Jehu, and Jehu was the father of Azariah.

L.38: And Obed begot Jehu, and Jehu begot Azariah.

R.38: Obed was the father of Jehu, and Jehu was the father of Azariah.

decisions.reason: Not the kings of those names; both were common names.

records.source: וַעֲזַרְיָה֙ הֹלִ֣יד אֶת־חָ֔לֶץ וְחֶ֖לֶץ הֹלִ֥יד אֶת־אֶלְעָשָֽׂה׃

pieces: Azariah was the father of Helez, and Helez was the father of Eleasah.

L.39: And Azariah begot Helez, and Helez begot Eleasah.

R.39: Azariah was the father of Helez, and Helez was the father of Eleasah.

decisions.reason: As in verse 10: the same wording for this formula throughout the family lists.

pieces: Eleasah was the father of Sismai, and Sismai was the father of Shallum.

L.40: And Eleasah begot Sismai, and Sismai begot Shallum.

R.40: Eleasah was the father of Sismai, and Sismai was the father of Shallum.

decisions.reason: As in verse 10: the same wording for this formula throughout the family lists.

records.gloss: And Shallum begot Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begot Elishama.
pieces: Shallum was the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.

L.41: And Shallum begot Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begot Elishama.

R.41: Shallum was the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.

decisions.reason: Sheshan's line through his daughter runs thirteen generations, from Attai to Elishama, one of the longest unbroken lines in these lists. It shows that a family with no sons was not cut off.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֤י כָלֵב֙ אֲחִ֣י יְרַחְמְאֵ֔ל מֵישָׁ֥ע בְּכֹר֖וֹ ה֣וּא אֲבִי־זִ֑יף וּבְנֵ֥י מָרֵשָׁ֖ה אֲבִ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Caleb, brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, he [was the] father of Ziph; and [the] sons of Mareshah, father of Hebron.
pieces: The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.

L.42: And [the] sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, he [was the] father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.

R.42: The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, were Mesha, his oldest son, who was the founder of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the founder of Hebron.

alternatives: Mareshah, his second son, the father of Hebron
decisions.reason: The words are hard to fit: one expects a second son of Caleb, not "the sons of" someone. The early Greek translation reads differently here, and something may have dropped out of the Hebrew. The Hebrew text is followed.

Caleb here is Caleb son of Hezron (verses 9, 18). Ziph, Mareshah and Hebron are towns of Judah (Joshua 15:44, 54-55). Hebron was given to Caleb son of Jephunneh (Joshua 14:13-14), so the lists join the families of the two Calebs (see verse 18).
As in verse 24: Readable explains "father of" a town.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י חֶבְר֑וֹן קֹ֥רַח וְתַפֻּ֖חַ וְרֶ֥קֶם וָשָֽׁמַע׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Hebron: Korah and Tappuah and Rekem and Shema.
pieces: The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem and Shema.

L.43: And [the] sons of Hebron: Korah and Tappuah and Rekem and Shema.

R.43: The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem and Shema.

decisions.reason: Hebron is here the son of Mareshah (verse 42). Some of his sons' names are also names of towns (Tappuah, Joshua 15:34). This Korah is not the Levite of Numbers 16.

records.source: וְשֶׁ֣מַע הוֹלִ֔יד אֶת־רַ֖חַם אֲבִ֣י יָרְקֳעָ֑ם וְרֶ֖קֶם הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־שַׁמָּֽי׃

pieces: Shema was the father of Raham the father of Jorkeam, and Rekem was the father of Shammai.

L.44: And Shema begot Raham the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem begot Shammai.

R.44: Shema was the father of Raham, the founder of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.

decisions.reason: As in verse 24. Jorkeam is a town not named elsewhere.
As in verse 24: Readable explains "father of" a town.

records.gloss: And [the] son of Shammai: Maon; and Maon [was the] father of Beth-zur.
pieces: The son of Shammai: Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.

L.45: And [the] son of Shammai: Maon; and Maon [was the] father of Beth-zur.

R.45: Shammai's son was Maon, the founder of Beth-zur.

decisions.choice: Maon and Beth-zur: towns of Caleb's people
decisions.reason: Maon and Beth-zur are towns in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:55, 58). Nabal of Maon was a Calebite (1 Samuel 25:2-3).
As in verse 24: Readable explains "father of" a town.

records.source: וְעֵיפָה֙ פִּילֶ֣גֶשׁ כָּלֵ֔ב יָֽלְדָ֛ה אֶת־חָרָ֥ן וְאֶת־מוֹצָ֖א וְאֶת־גָּזֵ֑ז וְחָרָ֖ן הֹלִ֥יד אֶת־גָּזֵֽז׃ס
records.gloss: And Ephah, concubine of Caleb, bore Haran and Moza and Gazez; and Haran begot Gazez.
pieces: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.

L.46: And Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran and Moza and Gazez; and Haran begot Gazez.

R.46: Caleb also had a concubine (a secondary wife) named Ephah. She had three sons, Haran, Moza and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.

decisions.choice: concubine: a wife of lower rank
decisions.reason: A concubine was a woman joined to a man as a wife but with lower standing than a full wife; her children belonged to his family.

decisions.choice: two men named Gazez, or one
decisions.reason: Gazez is named as Ephah's son and then as Haran's son. Either Haran named his son after his brother, or the last clause repeats the name by a slip; the text does not say.
Readable explains the word concubine, as at Judges 19:1.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י יָהְדָּ֑י רֶ֧גֶם וְיוֹתָ֛ם וְגֵישָׁ֥ן וָפֶ֖לֶט וְעֵיפָ֥ה וָשָֽׁעַף׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Jahdai: Regem and Jotham and Geshan and Pelet and Ephah and Shaaph.
pieces: The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.

L.47: And [the] sons of Jahdai: Regem and Jotham and Geshan and Pelet and Ephah and Shaaph.

R.47: The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.

decisions.choice: Jahdai: not linked to the line
decisions.reason: The list does not say who Jahdai was or how he joined Caleb's family; he may be another of Caleb's sons or wives. Ephah is here a man's name, the same as the name of the concubine in verse 46.

records.source: פִּלֶ֤גֶשׁ כָּלֵב֙ מַעֲכָ֔ה יָ֥לַד שֶׁ֖בֶר וְאֶֽת־תִּרְחֲנָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] concubine of Caleb, Maacah, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
pieces: Maacah, Caleb's concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.

L.48: Caleb's concubine Maacah bore Sheber and Tirhanah.

R.48: Caleb had another concubine, Maacah. She had two sons, Sheber and Tirhanah.

decisions.choice: bore: the verb form is masculine
decisions.reason: The verb is written in the masculine form, though Maacah is its subject; the next verse has the feminine. The sense is not in doubt.
Readable links Maacah to Ephah (verse 46) and explains the word as there.

records.source: וַתֵּ֗לֶד שַׁ֚עַף אֲבִ֣י מַדְמַנָּ֔ה אֶת־שְׁוָ֛א אֲבִ֥י מַכְבֵּנָ֖ה וַאֲבִ֣י גִבְעָ֑א וּבַת־כָּלֵ֖ב עַכְסָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And she bore Shaaph, father of Madmannah, Sheva, father of Machbenah and father of Gibea. And [the] daughter of Caleb [was] Achsah.
pieces: She also bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and of Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.

L.49: And she bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea. And the daughter of Caleb [was] Achsah.

R.49: She also had Shaaph, the founder of Madmannah, and Sheva, the founder of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.

decisions.choice: Achsah: the name of the daughter of Caleb son of Jephunneh
decisions.reason: Caleb son of Jephunneh gave his daughter Achsah to Othniel (Joshua 15:16-17; Judges 1:12-13). The list here gives a daughter of the same name to the earlier Caleb's family. Whether it treats the two Calebs as one family, it does not say (see verse 18).

decisions.choice: Madmannah, Machbenah, Gibea: towns of Judah
decisions.reason: Madmannah is in the south of Judah (Joshua 15:31); Gibea may be Gibeah of the hill country (Joshua 15:57).
As in verse 24: Readable explains "father of" a town.

records.source: אֵ֤לֶּה הָיוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י כָלֵ֔ב בֶּן־ח֖וּר בְּכ֣וֹר אֶפְרָ֑תָה שׁוֹבָ֕ל אֲבִ֖י קִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: These were [the] sons of Caleb. [The] son of Hur, [the] firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal, father of Kiriath-jearim,
pieces: These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim,

L.50: These were the sons of Caleb. [The] son of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim,

R.50: These were Caleb's descendants. Hur was the oldest son of Ephrathah. His sons were Shobal, the founder of Kiriath-jearim,

decisions.choice: These were the sons of Caleb. The son of Hur ...
alternatives: These were the sons of Caleb son of Hur
decisions.reason: Word for word the Hebrew can be read "the sons of Caleb son of Hur". But Hur is Caleb's son (verse 19), and Ephrath(ah) is Hur's mother, so the sentence is read as closing Caleb's list, with "son of Hur" opening a new one. The early Greek translation reads it the same way.
Balanced and Readable say "descendants" in the closing line, as in verse 33, and "sons" for Hur's, since three are named (verses 50-51).

records.source: שַׂלְמָא֙ אֲבִ֣י בֵֽית־לָ֔חֶם חָרֵ֖ף אֲבִ֥י בֵית־גָּדֵֽר׃
records.gloss: Salma, father of Bethlehem, Hareph, father of Beth-gader.
pieces: Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader.

L.51: Salma the father of Bethlehem, Hareph the father of Beth-gader.

R.51: Salma, the founder of Bethlehem, and Hareph, the founder of Beth-gader.

decisions.reason: Bethlehem was the town of Ephrathah (Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:1), and David's family came from it. Salma is also the name of Boaz's father (verse 11); whether the two are one man is not said.
As in verse 24: Readable explains "father of" a town.

records.source: וַיִּהְי֤וּ בָנִים֙ לְשׁוֹבָ֔ל אֲבִ֖י קִרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֑ים הָרֹאֶ֖החֲצִ֥י הַמְּנֻחֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And were sons to Shobal, father of Kiriath-jearim: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth.
pieces: Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim had descendants: Haroeh, half of the Manahathites.

L.52: And Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Manahathites.

R.52: Shobal, the founder of Kiriath-jearim, had descendants: Haroeh and half of the Manahathites.

alternatives: Haroeh, head of half the Manahathites
decisions.reason: Haroeh ("the seer") is probably Reaiah son of Shobal (4:2). The Manahathites (here spelled Menuhoth) seem to be a clan, half of which traced its descent from Shobal and half from Salma (verse 54). The words may also mean that Haroeh was the head of that half.
"Sons" here covers a person and a clan, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants".
As in verse 24: Readable explains "father of" a town.

records.source: וּמִשְׁפְּחוֹת֙ קִרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֔ים הַיִּתְרִי֙ וְהַפּוּתִ֔י וְהַשֻּׁמָתִ֖י וְהַמִּשְׁרָעִ֑י מֵאֵ֗לֶּה יָצְאוּ֙ הַצָּ֣רְעָתִ֔י וְהָאֶשְׁתָּ֖אֻֽלִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] clans of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites and the Puthites and the Shumathites and the Mishraites; from these went out the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
pieces: The clans of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites and the Mishraites. From these came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.

L.53: And [the] clans of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites and the Puthites and the Shumathites and the Mishraites; from these went out the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.

R.53: The clans of Kiriath-jearim were the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites and Mishraites. The people of Zorah and Eshtaol came from these clans.

decisions.choice: Zorathites and Eshtaolites: the people of Zorah and Eshtaol
decisions.reason: Zorah and Eshtaol are towns in the lowland west of Kiriath-jearim (Joshua 15:33), the home country of Samson (Judges 13:2, 25). Two of David's warriors were Ithrites (2 Samuel 23:38).

decisions.choice: the people of Zorah and Eshtaol
decisions.reason: Readable names the towns behind the clan names.

records.source: בְּנֵ֣י שַׂלְמָ֗א בֵּ֥ית לֶ֨חֶם֙ וּנְט֣וֹפָתִ֔י עַטְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית יוֹאָ֑ב וַחֲצִ֥י הַמָּנַחְתִּ֖י הַצָּרְעִֽי׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Salma: Bethlehem and [the] Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.
pieces: The descendants of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.

L.54: [The] sons of Salma: Bethlehem and [the] Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.

R.54: The descendants of Salma were the people of Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.

decisions.choice: sons of Salma: towns and clans
decisions.reason: The "sons" are the towns and clans that traced their descent from Salma. Netophah was a village near Bethlehem (Ezra 2:21-22; 2 Samuel 23:28). The Zorites are probably the Zorathites of verse 53.
As in verse 52.

records.source: וּמִשְׁפְּח֤וֹת סֹפְרִים֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יַעְבֵּ֔ץ תִּרְעָתִ֥ים שִׁמְעָתִ֖ים שׂוּכָתִ֑ים הֵ֚מָּה הַקִּינִ֣ים הַבָּאִ֔ים מֵחַמַּ֖ת אֲבִ֥י בֵית־רֵכָֽב׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] clans of scribes dwelling [at] Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites. They [were] the Kenites who came from Hammath, father of [the] house of Rechab.
pieces: The clans of scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites and the Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.

L.55: And the clans of [the] scribes who dwelt [at] Jabez: [the] Tirathites, [the] Shimeathites, [the] Sucathites. These [are] the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.

R.55: Some families of scribes lived at Jabez. They were the Tirathites, Shimeathites and Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the ancestor of the family of Rechab.

decisions.choice: who lived: written and read forms
decisions.reason: The written text has "they lived"; the form read aloud is "those living". The sense is the same.

The word means scribes, people skilled in writing, but here it may be the name of a clan (Sophrites). Jabez is a place not named elsewhere, perhaps linked with the man Jabez of 4:9-10. What the three clan names mean is not known.

decisions.choice: the Kenites and the house of Rechab
alternatives: came from the town of Hammath
decisions.reason: The Kenites were the people of Moses' father-in-law who settled with Judah (Judges 1:16). The house of Rechab includes Jehonadab son of Rechab (2 Kings 10:15) and the Rechabites of Jeremiah 35. Hammath may be the ancestor's name or a place.
Readable explains "father of" a family by "ancestor".
